meta.title: Left–right self-placement
meta.question: Do Poles place themselves on the left or on the right?
meta.anchor: Read on the scale of CBOS's question asking people to mark their political views on a line from left-wing (1) to right-wing (7), in its face-to-face surveys, with every scale placed on 0 to 10.

items.wording: In political matters people talk of 'the left' and 'the right'. How would you place your views on this scale? (1 left, 10 right)
items.notes: EVS 1990, 1999, 2008, 2017 (4). Read by 18_more_microdata.R through the generic readers (data-raw/items_more.csv).

items.wording: On this line, points mark different political views, from left-wing to right-wing. Which point best matches your own views? (1 left-wing, 7 right-wing)
items.notes: The anchor: the trend is read on this question's scale. CBOS's monthly face-to-face surveys (Aktualne problemy i wydarzenia).

items.wording: CBOS_LR collapsed as CBOS's reports print it: left-wing (1-3) 0, centre (4) 5, right-wing (5-7) 10
items.notes: Read from every CBOS microdata survey (face to face), and from 2018 to April 2020 from the "Poglądy polityczne" block that ends almost every annex table of CBOS's reports (weighted counts of the whole sample; 13_cbos_reports.R). Its own level and sensitivity: a three-category mean is not the 1-7 mean.

items.wording: In political matters people talk of 'the left' and 'the right'. How would you place your views on this scale? (1 left, 10 right)
items.notes: Central and Eastern Eurobarometer 1-3 (1990-92).

items.wording: Left-right self-placement (1 left, 10 right)
items.notes: Consolidation of Democracy in Central and Eastern Europe, January 1991 and March 2000.

items.wording: Left-right self-placement of one's political views (1 left-wing, 10 right-wing)
items.notes: Polish General Social Survey, ten waves 1992-2010. In 1997-2002 asked of about half the sample.

items.notes: Polish National Election Study, 1997-2023 (harmonised master file).

items.notes: Pew 2002 (Poland n=500). Read by 18_more_microdata.R through the generic readers (data-raw/items_more.csv).

items.wording: In politics people sometimes talk of 'left' and 'right'. Where would you place yourself on this scale, where 0 means the left and 10 means the right?
items.notes: European Social Survey rounds 1-11 (2002-23), respondents aged 18 and over.

items.wording: In political matters people talk of 'the left' and 'the right'. How would you place your views on this scale? (1 left, 10 right)

items.wording: In political matters people talk of 'the left' and 'the right'. How would you place your views on this scale? (1 left, 10 right)
items.notes: Standard, Special and European Parliament Eurobarometers, 2004-19, when 22-38% of Polish respondents gave no position (2-7% from 2020), so these waves have their own level.

items.wording: As above on a six-point scale (1 extreme left, 6 extreme right)
items.notes: Pew 2007 and 2008 (2008's second copy, Q94, not asked in Poland; the regex leaves it out). Not asked in Poland 2009-11. Read by 18_more_microdata.R through the generic readers (data-raw/items_more.csv).

items.wording: In political matters people talk of 'the left' and 'the right'. What is your position? (0 left, 10 right)
items.notes: EES 2009 and 2019. Read by 18_more_microdata.R through the generic readers (data-raw/items_more.csv).

items.wording: On a left-right scale from 0 to 6, with 0 extreme left and 6 extreme right, where would you place yourself?
items.notes: Pew 2012-19 and 2022-25, 12 surveys in Poland (2010 and 2011 not asked there). 2025 was by telephone (face to face before), so it should be a mode split of its own, as ESS round 10 is. 2018's ends are labelled only '0' and '6'. Read by 18_more_microdata.R through the generic readers (data-raw/items_more.csv).

items.wording: As above, 0-10 coded 1-11
